english.title: Unlawful disclosure of HMRC information re registration
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), having received information from His Majesty’s Revenue and Customs, further disclosed the revenue and customs information relating to **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), a person whose identity was specified in the information or could be deduced from it, otherwise than for the taking of an action in connection with an offence under Part 1 of the Economic Crime (Transparency and Enforcement) Act 2022
english.legislation: Contrary to section 40(4) of the Economic Crime (Transparency and Enforcement) Act 2022 and section 19(4) of the Commissioners for Revenue and Customs Act 2005.
english.pointstoprove: date and locationhaving received information from His Majesty's Revenue and Customs relating to a person specified in it or could be deduced from itdisclosed that informationotherwise than for the taking of an action in connection with an offence under Part 1 of the Economic Crime (Transparency and Enforcement) Act 2022

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
It is a defence under section 40(5) that the person reasonably believed —
(a) that the disclosure was lawful, or
(b) that the information had already lawfully been made available to the public.

other.penalty:
Either way -

Summary: maximum 12 months imprisonment and / or a fine. Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and / or fine

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

Note
The maximum penalty on summary conviction increased from 2nd May 2022. This applies only to offences committed on or after that date. For offences committed before 2nd May 2022 the maximum penalty on summary conviction is six months.
